title: Scripture Quiz Whisper
subject: Torts
stem:
Daniel first learned of Martha’s accusation when Martha later apologized to him. At a privately run Bible-character board-game tournament, Martha had pulled Lydia behind the prize table and falsely whispered, “Daniel is secretly swapping the Scripture-quiz answer cards.” Lydia kept the accusation to herself. Daniel sued Martha for false light.

Is Daniel likely to prevail on false light?
call: Is Daniel likely to prevail on false light?

choices.A: No, because false light requires commercial use of Daniel's identity.
choices.B: No, because the accusation was not publicized to a broad enough audience.
choices.C: Yes, because the accusation cast Daniel in a false light.
choices.D: Yes, because false light and defamation are the same tort.

rightExplanation:
B is correct. Martha made the accusation only to Lydia, in a private aside, and Lydia kept it to herself. Daniel has a false-light theory only if the false light was publicized to the public or to a broad enough audience. That publicity threshold is missing.

Gold Key: False light needs public-style publicity. A private one-listener accusation is not enough, even if the statement is false and offensive.

Silver Key: In a No/No pair, keep the No reason that tracks the decisive fact in the stem. Here the repeated fact is the private one-person communication, not commercial use.

c3.label: CUT A
c3.text: Wrong-frame / bait-doctrine. It gives the right kind of No outcome but uses the wrong privacy tort. Commercial use belongs to appropriation, not false light.

c3.label: CUT C
c3.text: Wrong-element. It proves only the false-impression piece. It does not answer the publicity threshold.

c3.label: CUT D
c3.text: Flat misstatement. “Same tort” collapses two neighboring doctrines into one.

c3.label: Residual B
c3.text: It is true and responsive once the Gold Key is applied. The stem gives one listener and no repeat.

c3.label: CLASH
c3.text: Not needed after the anchor-assisted Cut.

studentScript: False light. Private whisper to one person. Gold Key: false light needs publicity. Cut commercial-use as the wrong privacy tort, cut false-impression-only as missing publicity, cut defamation-same as a false collapse. B survives.

A.signal: The choice says No but gives an appropriation-style reason, not a false-light publicity reason.
A.lawyer: Commercial identity use is an appropriation/right-of-publicity concept; false light turns on publicity placing the plaintiff in a false light.

B.signal: This choice uses the exact stem facts: one private listener and no repeat.
B.lawyer: False light requires publicity; a private one-listener accusation is insufficient.

C.signal: The choice proves the tempting element but skips the audience gate.
C.lawyer: A false or misleading impression is not enough without false-light publicity.

D.signal: The word same is the danger word; the Gold Key keeps false light separate from defamation.
D.lawyer: False light overlaps with defamation but has distinct elements, including publicity and offensiveness.

goldKeys.statement: False light needs publicity to the public or a broad audience. A private one-listener accusation is not enough, even if it is false.
goldKeys.trigger: false light claim + one private listener + no repeat
goldKeys.authority: Restatement (Second) of Torts §652E; Restatement publicity commentary.

goldKeys.statement: Commercial use of a person's identity is appropriation, not false light. Do not borrow the neighboring privacy tort's element.
goldKeys.trigger: false light choice using identity, likeness, or commercial use

silverKeys.statement: When two answers say No, keep the No reason that matches the stem's decisive fact. Here, private audience beats commercial-use vocabulary.
silverKeys.trigger: two No choices in a privacy-tort element question
silverKeys.unlocks: No/No pair between false-light publicity and appropriation wrong-frame

remediation.title: False light publicity gate
remediation.signal: False-light claim after a private accusation.
remediation.studentMove: Ask whether the matter reached the public or a broad audience.
remediation.tinyRule: One private listener is not false-light publicity.
remediation.trap: Treating falsity or defamation overlap as enough.
